abstract: Microsoft's Work Trend Index survey of 31,000 workers across multiple countries finding that 75% of knowledge workers use AI tools at work and 78% bring their own AI tools (BYOAI) rather than relying on employer-provided solutions. The report highlights a significant gap between employee-driven AI adoption and organizational AI strategy, with workers adopting AI tools faster than IT departments can govern them.
keyFindings: 75% of knowledge workers report using AI at work
78% of AI-using workers bring their own AI tools (BYOAI) rather than using employer-provided options
Significant gap exists between bottom-up employee adoption and top-down organizational AI strategy
Workers report AI helps most with information synthesis, drafting, and meeting preparation
methodology: Large-scale survey of n=31,000 knowledge workers across multiple countries, conducted as part of Microsoft's annual Work Trend Index. Measures AI adoption rates, usage patterns, and organizational readiness through self-reported data.
qualifiers: Microsoft has commercial interest in promoting AI adoption narratives. Knowledge workers are not representative of the full workforce. Self-reported usage may conflate occasional experimentation with regular productive use. Survey conducted by an AI tool vendor.
